title: Regularity of the negative-degree and degree-zero ideal quotient at a homogeneous maximal ideal
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with a $\mathbf Z$-grading $A=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}A_n$: the $A_n$ are additive subgroups, every element has a unique finite homogeneous expansion, $1\in A_0$, and $A_iA_j\subseteq A_{i+j}$. Suppose $A_0$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_0$ (local means that this is its unique maximal ideal), and suppose the additive subgroup
$$\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_0\oplus\bigoplus_{n\ne0}A_n$$
is an ideal of $A$, hence a maximal ideal with residue field $A_0/\mathfrak m_0$. Let $\mathfrak a\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be a homogeneous ideal, meaning $\mathfrak a=\bigoplus_n(\mathfrak a\cap A_n)$, and put $\mathfrak a_0=\mathfrak a\cap A_0$ and
$$\mathfrak b=\left(\mathfrak a_0,\ \bigcup_{n<0}A_n\right)\subseteq\mathfrak m,$$
where parentheses denote the ideal generated by the indicated subsets. If the local rings $A_{\mathfrak m}$ and $(A/\mathfrak a)_{\mathfrak m/\mathfrak a}$ are regular local rings [def-weil-regular-scheme], then $(A/\mathfrak b)_{\mathfrak m/\mathfrak b}$ is a regular local ring. Localization at a prime inverts its complement [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Lemma 13.27 (Hesselink 1981, 5.6), printed p.263; standing graded-local hypotheses immediately preceding Lemma 13.25 on printed p.262. The homogeneous maximal-ideal hypothesis is explicit here.

proof.text: Put $R=A_{\mathfrak m}$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mR$, $I=\mathfrak aR$, and $\kappa=A/\mathfrak m=A_0/\mathfrak m_0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient], $R/I\simeq(A/\mathfrak a)_{\mathfrak m/\mathfrak a}$, so both $R$ and $R/I$ are regular local. Identify $V=\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ with $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$: the inverse on a fraction class $x/s$ is $\overline{s}^{-1}\overline{x}$. This is well defined because $\mathfrak m$ kills $V$ and every $s\notin\mathfrak m$ acts on $V$ by the nonzero residue $\overline{s}\in\kappa$. The same formula identifies the image $W=(\mathfrak a+\mathfrak m^2)/\mathfrak m^2$ with $(I+\mathfrak n^2)/\mathfrak n^2$.

source.place: Lemma 13.27, first paragraph, cotangent exact sequence; Stacks Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient) for the localization/quotient identification.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-cotangent-dimension], $V$ has finite dimension $d=\dim R$. The ideals $\mathfrak m$, $\mathfrak m^2$, and $\mathfrak a$ are homogeneous, and $\kappa$ is concentrated in degree zero; hence $V$ and its subspace $W$ are direct sums of their degree pieces. Choose bases of those pieces of $W$ and extend them to bases of the corresponding pieces of $V$. Lift the resulting homogeneous basis to $x_1,\ldots,x_d\in\mathfrak m$, taking $x_1,\ldots,x_r\in\mathfrak a$ for the basis of $W$, where $r=\dim_\kappa W$. Write $w_i=\deg x_i$. Only finitely many pieces are nonzero, since $V$ is finite dimensional.

source.place: Lemma 13.27, first paragraph, choice of the homogeneous cotangent basis adapted to the image of the ideal.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-quotient-independent-generators] to $I\subseteq\mathfrak n$. It supplies generators $s_j$ of $I$ with independent classes in $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$. Consequently $I\cap\mathfrak n^2=\mathfrak nI$: if $y=\sum a_js_j$ lies in $\mathfrak n^2$, independence gives $a_j\in\mathfrak n$, and the reverse inclusion is immediate. Thus $I/\mathfrak nI\to\mathfrak n/\mathfrak n^2$ is injective with image $W$. The classes of $x_1/1,\ldots,x_r/1$ therefore form a basis of $I/\mathfrak nI$. The ring $R$ is Noetherian by regularity, so its ideals $I$ and $\mathfrak n$ are finite. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] to each: $I=(x_1/1,\ldots,x_r/1)$ and $\mathfrak n=(x_1/1,\ldots,x_d/1)$.

source.place: Lemma 13.27, second paragraph, identifying the ideal generated by the chosen parameters; Stacks Tag 00NR (lemma-regular-quotient-regular) and Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK).

proof.text:

otin\mathfrak m$ by the fraction relation. Taking the component of degree $\deg h$ gives $s_0h\in J$. Since $s
otin\mathfrak m$, $s_0
otin\mathfrak m_0$, so $s_0$ is a unit of the local ring $A_0$ and $h\in J$. Finite homogeneous expansion now gives $H=J$. This is the explicit component argument of Milne 13.25--13.26, rather than an appeal to a separate graded Nakayama theorem.

source.place: Lemmas 13.25--13.26, printed pp.262--263; Lemma 13.27, second paragraph, global equality of the homogeneous ideals.

proof.text: Let $J$ be generated by those $x_i$ with $w_i<0$, together with those $x_i$ with $i\le r$ and $w_i=0$. Every generator belongs to $\mathfrak b$, so $J\subseteq\mathfrak b$. For homogeneous $h\in A_n$ with $n<0$, the equality $\mathfrak m=(x_1,\ldots,x_d)$ gives $h=\sum_i c_ix_i$ with each $c_i$ homogeneous of degree $n-w_i$ (take that component of each coefficient). If $w_i<0$, the term lies in $J$; otherwise $n-w_i<0$, so $c_i\in\mathfrak b$ and $x_i\in\mathfrak m$, and the term lies in $\mathfrak m\mathfrak b$. Thus $A_n\subseteq J+\mathfrak m\mathfrak b$ for every $n<0$.

source.place: Lemma 13.27, third and fourth paragraphs: the selected parameter ideal and the negative-degree calculation.

proof.text: For $h\in\mathfrak a_0$, the equality $\mathfrak a=(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ gives $h=\sum_{i\le r}c_ix_i$ with $c_i\in A_{-w_i}$. If $w_i\le0$, then $x_i\in J$; if $w_i>0$, then $c_i$ has negative degree, hence lies in $\mathfrak b$, and $c_ix_i\in\mathfrak m\mathfrak b$. Therefore $\mathfrak a_0\subseteq J+\mathfrak m\mathfrak b$. Along with step 5 and the definition of $\mathfrak b$, this gives $\mathfrak b=J+\mathfrak m\mathfrak b$.

source.place: Lemma 13.27, final paragraph: the nonpositive-degree equation calculation, here applied to the degree-zero generators defining the item.

proof.text: Since $A$ is Noetherian, $\mathfrak b$ is finitely generated, so $\mathfrak bR$ is a finite $R$-module. Localize step 6 to get $\mathfrak bR=JR+\mathfrak n(\mathfrak bR)$. The submodule form of [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] gives $\mathfrak bR=JR$. The $d$ elements $x_i/1$ form a regular system of parameters of $R$, by steps 2--3. Reorder this list with the generators defining $J$ first and apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence]: its initial-quotient clause gives that $R/JR$ is regular local, including when the selected set is empty. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient] identifies $R/JR=R/\mathfrak bR$ with $(A/\mathfrak b)_{\mathfrak m/\mathfrak b}$, which proves the assertion.

source.place: Lemma 13.27, third paragraph and conclusion; Stacks Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), Tag 00NQ (lemma-regular-ring-CM), and Tag 00CT (proposition-localize-quotient).

proof_origin.place: Lemmas 13.25--13.27, printed pp.262--263; the regular-quotient parameter input is Stacks Tag 00NR, and the final comparison is localized before applying Nakayama.

lean.statement: theorem graded_local_attraction_regularity (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A] (𝒜 : ℤ → AddSubgroup A) [GradedRing 𝒜] [IsLocalRing (𝒜 0)] (m : Ideal A) [m.IsMaximal] (hm : ∀ x : A, x ∈ m ↔ DirectSum.decompose 𝒜 x 0 ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (𝒜 0)) (a : Ideal A) (ha : a.IsHomogeneous 𝒜) (ham : a ≤ m) (b : Ideal A) (hb : b = Ideal.span ({x : A | x ∈ a ∧ x ∈ 𝒜 0} ∪ {x : A | ∃ n : ℤ, n < 0 ∧ x ∈ 𝒜 n})) [IsRegularLocalRing (Localization.AtPrime m)] [IsRegularLocalRing (Localization (m.primeCompl.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk a)))] : IsRegularLocalRing (Localization (m.primeCompl.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk b)))
lean.note: The degree-zero projection characterizes the stipulated homogeneous maximal ideal. Quotient localizations invert the image of m.primeCompl, exactly the complement of m/a or m/b because a and b lie in m. No new notion or statement correction.
